discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (moire materials, flat-band superconductivity)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate over kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers realised this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This theory-experiment pair opened an entirely new field, twistronics and moire quantum matter, providing a tunable platform in which band structure, filling and interactions are controlled by a gate voltage and twist angle. The prediction has been confirmed across many systems: twisted multilayer graphene, transition-metal dichalcogenide moire materials hosting fractional Chern insulators, and Wigner crystals. The work revealed that superconductivity in flat bands is governed by quantum geometry of Bloch states, linking band topology to superfluidity. Few discoveries of the past decade have so reshaped condensed matter physics.
